cover.headline: OpenRouter pulled *125* endpoints from zero data retention.
cover.sub: After canary keys caught attackers inside three AI hosts. Three changes from 21 to 23 Nov on controls for agents, plus two courses.

items.title: OpenRouter pulled *125* endpoints from zero retention
items.statLabel: endpoints lost zero data retention eligibility, some as a precaution
items.what: Dragos hid canary keys in about 2 million prompts and caught attackers inside 3 AI hosts. On 22 Nov OpenRouter dropped 3 providers.
items.why: Some stolen requests were flagged zero retention. Keep secrets out of prompts, pick providers yourself and plant canaries in your own traffic.

items.title: Claude Ship lets an agent *approve* pull requests
items.statLabel: required GitHub approval that Claude's own review can fill, per the docs
items.what: In beta from 23 Nov for Team and Enterprise on GitHub. Approvals follow a policy file in the repo. PR Steward fixes failing checks but can't approve.
items.why: Anyone who can merge the policy file can switch approvals on. Protect it, keep CI and a secrets scan required, and start in observe mode.

items.title: Banks now give their own AI agents *staff rules*
items.statLabel: agents brought into identity and access management, per Reuters' sources
items.what: Reuters, 23 Nov: US banks are limiting what internal agents reach, logging what each did and whether a person approved it, and reviewing kill switches.
items.why: If you sell AI to banks, expect a credential per agent, logs it can't edit, a tested off switch and a manual fallback. Sources are anonymous.

coursesTitle: Learn the *attacker's* side, then the controls

courses.title: Learn Real-World Penetration Testing
courses.note: freeCodeCamp, taught by Declan Middleton, posted 29 Oct. About 2.5 hours on a practice target: Nmap, hidden endpoints, Burp Suite, scripted recon.

courses.title: Governing AI Agents
courses.note: Built with Databricks, 1h30m: give an agent its own identity, only the data it needs, and logs of what it did. Updated 17 Jul, so not new.

read: OpenRouter will test the *network path* before zero retention comes back. Anthropic made approval a *file* you can protect. Banks gave agents *their own keys* and logs they can't edit.
takeaway: Swap each label you rely on for a check you can run: a canary, a protected approvals file, a log your agent can't edit.
